label: Person
name: Adolph John Paschang
summary:
Adolph John Paschang (1887–1968) was an American Maryknoll missionary bishop who served in China and later as a mission administrator, representing the generation of American Catholic missionaries whose extraordinary work in China was abruptly terminated by the Communist revolution in 1949. Born in Missouri, he joined the newly founded Maryknoll Society and was sent to China, where he eventually became a vicar apostolic.

Paschang worked in Jilin province in Manchuria, a region that passed through the upheavals of Japanese occupation (1931–1945), Soviet intervention, and Communist consolidation. He was expelled from China after the Communist victory in 1949–1950 along with all other foreign missionaries. The Maryknoll expulsion from China was one of the defining traumas of American Catholic missionary history, abruptly ending decades of institutional building.

After his expulsion, Paschang served in administrative roles for Maryknoll, helping to redirect the congregation's mission energy toward Latin America, Africa, and other regions. His generation of expelled China missionaries became the institutional memory of American Catholic engagement with East Asia, and many contributed to the eventual reopening of dialogue with Chinese Catholicism after Mao's death. He exemplifies the Maryknoll spirit of adaptable missionary commitment across changing geopolitical conditions.
